turns.text: Plants cannot walk to a new location, but their seeds can travel. Consider two strategies. Some seeds are light and have structures that help them float in the wind. These structures increase the surface area without adding much weight. Other seeds are enclosed in fruit. An animal eats the fruit and may carry the seeds away before dropping them. Both strategies can reduce competition between a young plant and its parent. However, neither guarantees that a seed will land in suitable soil. Wind direction is unpredictable, and animals do not choose their routes for the benefit of plants. Successful dispersal therefore depends on both a way to move and a favorable place to grow.

questions.prompt: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.text: Why all seeds need animal transport.

How plants choose an animal route.
Why wind cannot carry seeds.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about a seed that travels far from its parent?

options.text: It will always grow into a plant.
It must have been carried by an animal.
It still needs suitable growing conditions.
It can no longer compete with any plant.

feedback.q1: The lecturer explains wind transport and animal transport as two ways seeds disperse.
feedback.q2: The lecturer distinguishes movement from successful growth. A favorable place to grow is still necessary.
